archetypes.name: Process / Oil & Gas Facility
civil_interfaces: equipment foundations and anchor-bolt setting for vessels/compressors
bunded tank farm slabs and containment
commissioning_focus: mechanical completion by system/subsystem then loop checks
hydrotest and reinstatement of process piping
rotating-equipment run-in (pumps/compressors) with alignment and vibration
N2 purge / leak test / dry-out before hydrocarbon introduction
firewater ring and deluge functional test
SIS/ESD loop and cause-effect proving before first feed
archetypes.notes: Piping-dominant EPC. Spool fabrication + rotating equipment + tanks/vessels are the schedule drivers; commissioning is system/subsystem-based (mechanical completion → loop → start-up), not area-based. Insulation/coating and heat-tracing sit on the critical path to weatherization. Hazardous-area electrical and firewater/deluge are safety-critical and gate start-up.

archetypes.name: Chemical / Petrochemical / Refinery Complex
civil_interfaces: heavy reactor/column foundations and pile caps
tank farm bunds and impervious liners
underground process sewers and effluent/neutralization networks
commissioning_focus: subsystem mechanical completion → loop check → pre-commissioning
utility-first sequence (steam, N2, instrument air, cooling water) before process
tightness/leak test and passivation of alloy piping
distributed control system (DCS/SIS) integration and interlock proving
archetypes.notes: Like oil & gas but denser process piping, more alloy/exotic metallurgy driving spool fab lead times, and heavy insulation/heat-tracing scope. Utilities (steam, cooling water, instrument air, N2) must be commissioned first — utility-block readiness is the gating milestone. Effluent/neutralization and flare systems are compliance-critical.

archetypes.name: Power Generation / Utility Plant
civil_interfaces: turbine/generator pedestal and heavy machine foundations
underground cable trenches and earthing grid
commissioning_focus: boiler/HRSG hydrotest, chemical clean and steam blow
turbine-generator run-up, overspeed and vibration proving
high-voltage energization, protection and synchronization to grid
first fire → first sync → reliability/performance run
archetypes.notes: Rotating machinery (turbine-generator) and high-voltage electrical dominate. The earthing grid and HV protection/energization are first-class, not secondary MEP. Commissioning is a long, tightly-sequenced chain (steam blow → first fire → sync → reliability run) that owns the back end of the schedule. Applies to gas, steam, combined-cycle and large renewables/BESS interconnection.

archetypes.name: Water / Wastewater Treatment Plant
civil_interfaces: large water-retaining concrete structures (tanks, basins, clarifiers) with watertightness
buried inlet/outlet and interconnecting process pipelines
pump-station wet wells and dry wells
cable and duct banks to MCC/control building
commissioning_focus: clean-water functional run of pumps, blowers, valves and dosing
process/biological seeding and dirty-water commissioning to consent
SCADA/PLC loop checks and telemetry integration
archetypes.notes: Civil-heavy: watertight concrete basins and buried pipework are the enabling long-lead scope, so civil_interface is nearly a primary system here. Pumps, blowers, dosing skids and instrumentation are the mechanical core. Two-stage commissioning (clean-water then dirty/biological seeding) with a regulatory consent gate is characteristic and back-loaded.

archetypes.name: Heavy Industrial Factory / Process Plant
civil_interfaces: heavy machine/press foundations with isolation and inertia blocks
crane rail and portal-frame steel foundations
commissioning_focus: utility readiness (power, compressed air, cooling, steam) before line energization
individual machine/skid FAT-to-SAT and dry runs
conveyor and material-handling line integration and interlocks
production-line integrated run and no-load → loaded ramp-up
archetypes.notes: First-class industrial archetype: mixed process + discrete equipment tied together by conveying/material-handling and packaged skids. Structural steel (portal frames, mezzanines, crane rails) and heavy machine foundations are enablers on the critical path. Commissioning is line/cell-based with a no-load → loaded production ramp; utilities must land first. Sits between pure process plants and light manufacturing.

archetypes.name: Light / Discrete Manufacturing & Assembly Plant
civil_interfaces: level power-floated production slabs to tight flatness tolerance
service trenches and floor ducts for utilities
commissioning_focus: clean/dry utilities to point of use (power, air, water, exhaust)
machine SAT, conveyor/AGV line integration and interlock testing
HVAC/environmental control balance and (if applicable) cleanroom qualification
line integrated dry run then production ramp-up
archetypes.notes: Lighter than the heavy industrial factory: process piping is minor, but material handling (conveyors/AGVs), packaged machines and HVAC/environmental control dominate. Floor flatness and equipment plinths are key civil enablers. For pharma/food/electronics variants, HVAC becomes cleanroom qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and moves toward primary.

archetypes.name: Silo / Grain / Bulk Materials Terminal
civil_interfaces: deep silo raft/pile foundations and slip-formed or bolted silo civils
commissioning_focus: conveyor and transfer-chute belt run, tracking and no-load proving
elevator/bucket and diverter interlock and sequencing test
no-load → loaded bulk-flow trial and throughput verification
archetypes.notes: Bulk-handling archetype dominated by conveying, silos/tanks as storage vessels, and structural steel galleries/towers. No process piping to speak of; instrumentation centres on level/weight/flow. Dust explosion protection (venting/suppression) and earthing are safety-critical. Deep silo foundations are the long-lead civil enabler. Commissioning is a bulk-flow throughput trial, not a chemical start-up.

archetypes.name: Rail / Metro / Transit System
civil_interfaces: trackbed, tunnels, viaducts and station box civils
traction power substation foundations and cable routes
signalling equipment room and trackside cabinet bases
commissioning_focus: signalling/CBTC integration, interlocking and train-detection proving
tunnel ventilation and life-safety (fire/smoke) system proving
trial running, dynamic testing and system-integration/safety-case sign-off
archetypes.notes: Systems archetype where power (traction/aux), signalling (instrumentation), cabling containment and earthing/bonding dominate over process/mechanical scope. Conveying appears as escalators/lifts. Commissioning is dominated by signalling integration and a long trial-running / safety-case regime — the true schedule and risk driver. Deep civil (tunnels, station boxes, viaducts) is the enabling backbone.

archetypes.name: Data Center / Mission-Critical Facility
civil_interfaces: generator, transformer and chiller-yard foundations and bunds
raised-floor / slab flatness and equipment plinths
utility duct banks and incoming HV routes
commissioning_focus: Level 1–5 commissioning (factory → site → integrated systems test)
utility → generator → UPS → PDU power-path proving with load banks
chilled-water and CRAC/CRAH cooling capacity and redundancy (N+1) test
integrated systems test (IST) with black-building / failure-mode pull-the-plug
BMS/EPMS integration, VESDA and clean-agent fire suppression proving
archetypes.notes: Redundancy-and-resilience archetype: electrical power path (utility/gen/UPS/PDU) plus mechanical cooling (chilled water, CRAC/CRAH) are co-dominant, tied together by BMS/EPMS. Commissioning is the defining discipline — formal Level 1–5 with load-bank and integrated systems test / failure-mode proving that owns the back end. Fire (VESDA + clean agent) and structured cabling containment are first-class.

archetypes.name: Hospital / Healthcare Facility
civil_interfaces: plant-room and rooftop AHU/chiller structural provisions
medical-gas manifold room and bulk oxygen/tank compound civils
commissioning_focus: specialist HVAC balance and validation (operating theatres/isolation rooms, pressure cascades, HEPA)
medical gas pipeline system (MGPS) purity, pressure and alarm certification
essential/emergency power changeover and UPS proving
infection-control and clinical-area handover with regulatory sign-off
archetypes.notes: MEP-intensive critical facility. HVAC is primary and specialized (theatre air changes, pressure cascades, HEPA filtration validation) and medical-gas piping is a safety-critical variant of utility piping requiring formal certification. Redundant essential power and life-safety systems gate occupancy. Commissioning is validation-and-certification heavy with clinical handover, not industrial start-up.

archetypes.name: Commercial High-Rise / Mixed-Use Building
civil_interfaces: core walls, MEP riser shafts and floor penetrations
rooftop plant and cooling-tower structural provisions
commissioning_focus: vertical riser distribution (power, water, HVAC) proving floor-by-floor
lift/escalator installation, load and safety testing
fire detection, sprinkler, smoke-control and stair-pressurization cause-effect
BMS integration and integrated life-safety fire matrix test before occupancy
archetypes.notes: Vertical building archetype driven by MEP risers, vertical transportation (lifts/escalators as the conveying system) and life-safety (fire suppression, smoke control, stair pressurization). Commissioning centres on the integrated fire/life-safety cause-effect matrix that gates occupancy certificate. Structural steel/core is the enabler; process systems are absent.

archetypes.name: Linear / Civil Infrastructure (Roads, Bridges, Pipelines, Ports)
civil_interfaces: bridge and structure foundations, piers and deck civils
buried pipeline trenching, bedding and reinstatement
port/marine quay, jetty and dredging works
duct banks, chambers and cable/pipe crossings
commissioning_focus: structural load/proof testing and survey verification
pipeline hydrotest, pigging and cathodic-protection energization
roadside/tunnel M&E, lighting and ITS/SCADA integration
handover to operator against design and regulatory acceptance
archetypes.notes: Civil-dominant catch-all where earthworks, structures and buried networks are the primary scope and MEP is a lighter overlay (roadside/tunnel systems, ITS, lighting, pump stations). Pipeline variants pull in spool fabrication, hydrotest, pigging and cathodic protection. Commissioning is proof/acceptance testing and operator handover rather than a plant start-up. Use as the fallback archetype for linear and marine civil works.

archetypes.name: Residential Building (Generic)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Structure/blockwork → MEP first fix in walls & slab → plaster/board & waterproofing to wet areas → screed/tiling → second fix MEP → paint → joinery & sanitary fixtures → snagging → handover. Wet areas (bath/kitchen) gate the tiling and fixture chain.
archetypes.notes: Baseline residential template — apply when the schedule does not distinguish rise/typology. Finishing + light MEP first/second fix dominate the critical review; heavy plant/industrial systems are absent.

archetypes.name: Apartment Building
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Repetitive typical-floor cycle: unit blockwork → MEP first fix → wet-area waterproofing → screed & tiling → second fix → paint → joinery/sanitary → per-unit snag. Common cores (corridors, lobbies, risers) run as a parallel finishing front feeding vertical MEP.
archetypes.notes: Multi-unit repetition is the planning signature — typical-floor productivity and unit-to-unit handover cadence drive the programme. Risers and common-area MEP interface with every unit stack.

archetypes.name: Low-Rise Residential (G+1 to G+3)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Short vertical run, finishing-dominant: blockwork → MEP first fix → wet-area waterproofing → plaster → screed/tiling → second fix → paint → joinery & fixtures → snag. Roof waterproofing and external render gate weather-tightness.
archetypes.notes: Simpler, finishing-led with minimal vertical MEP coordination. No fire-fighting risers or lifts typically; commissioning is light and unit/floor-based.

archetypes.name: Mid-Rise Residential (G+4 to G+9)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Typical-floor repetition with an emerging vertical MEP spine: floor cycle feeds unit finishing (first fix → waterproofing → tiling → second fix → paint → joinery/fixtures) while cores, risers and stairs carry building-wide services. Fire alarm coverage becomes a coordinated floor-by-floor activity.
archetypes.notes: Transition band — finishing still dominates but vertical services (risers, fire alarm, lift-lobby MEP) start driving coordination. Life-safety commissioning appears but remains lighter than high-rise.

archetypes.name: High-Rise Residential (G+10 and above)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Core/jumpform leads, typical-floor finishing follows several floors below in a rolling wave. Vertical MEP spine (wet/dry risers, pump rooms, roof tanks, lift shafts) must be sequenced with the floor cycle; each unit still runs the first-fix→waterproofing→tiling→second-fix→fixtures chain, but building-wide life-safety and vertical transport gate handover.
archetypes.notes: Vertical MEP coordination dominates alongside finishing. Adds fire fighting (risers/sprinklers/pumps), fire alarm zoning, lifts, roof plant, and BMS-lite. Finishing is high-volume/repetitive but no longer the sole critical path — vertical services and life-safety commissioning share it.

archetypes.name: Residential Compound / Gated Community
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Repeated villa/townhouse type finished as a rolling front across plots, gated by site infrastructure (roads, utilities, external lighting). Each unit follows the villa finishing chain; landscaping, pools and boundary works close out the plot before community-level handover.
archetypes.notes: Horizontal repetition across many identical low-rise units plus shared site infrastructure. Planning signature is plot-by-plot productivity and utility/road enablement rather than vertical MEP. Commissioning is light and per-unit, with community-level utility and security systems layered on top.

archetypes.name: Townhouse (Attached Unit)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Attached low-rise unit, finishing-dominant: blockwork → MEP first fix → wet-area waterproofing → plaster → tiling → second fix → paint → joinery & fixtures → snag. Party-wall interface and shared services coordination with the adjacent unit is the only added complexity.
archetypes.notes: Essentially a villa in an attached row — simple, finishing-led, minimal commissioning. Repeats across a terrace; party-wall and shared-services coordination distinguish it from the standalone villa.

archetypes.name: Villa (Detached, High-Spec)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: High-spec finishing dominates the entire back half of the programme: blockwork → MEP first fix → wet-area/pool waterproofing → plaster → marble/stone tiling → second fix → paint → bespoke joinery → premium sanitary fixtures → intensive snagging. Stone/marble lead times and joinery quality gate handover.
archetypes.notes: Finishing-dominant with premium materials (marble, stone, bespoke joinery) — the review focus is the finishing-to-MEP interface and material lead times, not plant. Minimal industrial/commissioning content; often includes pool and landscape interfaces.

archetypes.name: Standalone House
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Simplest residential form: blockwork → MEP first fix → wet-area waterproofing → plaster → screed/tiling → second fix → paint → joinery & fixtures → snag. Roof waterproofing and external render gate weather-tightness before internal finishing accelerates.
archetypes.notes: Baseline single-dwelling template — finishing-led, minimal MEP coordination, light per-house commissioning. Use for detached houses without villa-grade material or pool/landscape complexity.

archetypes.name: Mixed-Use Residential (Residential over Retail/Podium)
archetypes.finishing_sequence_note: Two finishing regimes: retail/podium shell-and-core (often left as landlord shell) and the residential tower typical-floor finishing wave above. Vertical services must stay continuous through the transfer/podium level; residential units run the standard first-fix→waterproofing→tiling→second-fix→fixtures chain while podium and cores demand coordinated life-safety and MEP segregation.
archetypes.notes: Combines high-rise residential vertical MEP with a retail/podium interface. Review focus is the residential-to-commercial services segregation, transfer-level MEP continuity, and phased zoned handover (retail vs residential). Heaviest commissioning of the residential set due to shared life-safety and metering separation.
